atoms.reason: Full-proposal consensus (A/B/C). Multi-signal scope profile (acceptance_count, subsystem_count, estimated_turns) is a sounder classifier than a single heuristic, and retaining the atom/decomposed-child early-return preserves idempotency. Slightly more moving parts than the current heuristic costs simplicity, but the named inputs make it concrete and testable.

Consensus. Routing bridge-self decomposition through the existing Add-ProjectBacklogFromMarker(Channel='main') as the single ingest path, emitting [[PROJECT_BACKLOG]] JSON instead of raw Add-Idea, reuses a proven path and directly enables the consolidation in atom_08. High specificity (named function, channel, marker) and low integration risk.

Consensus. Making decomposition mandatory and blocking STATUS: CONTINUE when a large bridge-self parent lacks a valid split is the core safety invariant — it prevents the coder from being handed a monolith. Adds control-flow complexity (lower simplicity) and is low-reversibility, but the risk-reduction payoff is high. Depends on atom_06's split definition and atom_07's retry/hold to be complete.

penalties.reason: Unresolved gate-bypass tension with atom_10; 'bypassing approval/control-plane gates' overstates oversight removal

atoms.reason: Consensus on the automated-child mechanism (create approved, tag bridge-self, link via source_task_id). Conflicts head-on with atom_10. Resolve in favor of this atom because it aligns with consensus atom_08's 'no new gates', but MODIFY the wording: human oversight is not eliminated — it is preserved via atom_07's operator-hold on retry exhaustion, and the parent was already approved. State that children bypass only the per-decomposition re-approval, not all control-plane safety, which is why risk_reduction is scored moderate.

Consensus and the strongest atom. Fencing the entire mechanism to channel=='main'/scope=='bridge' and leaving Start-ProjectAutopilotIfNeeded and F1–F4 untouched is the critical blast-radius control that makes every other atom safe to ship. Low cost, high reversibility, and directly testable via PROJECT-channel non-interference.

Strong consensus (A/B). Defining 'valid split' deterministically from the ingest return value (created>=2, empty errors, single target file, concrete acceptance/checks, parent linkage) rather than re-scanning tags removes a fragile, race-prone check and gives atom_03 a precise gate condition. Highly specific; modest validation-logic cost lowers simplicity slightly.

From B only, but it completes atom_03: a bounded retry (2–3 attempts) that feeds deterministic ingest errors back into the retry prompt, then transitions to operator-hold and never falls back to coding the monolith. This is also the clean reconciliation point for the atom_04/atom_10 conflict — the human touchpoint lives here (hold on exhaustion) instead of a per-decomposition gate. Adds a loop and a hold state, costing simplicity.

Consensus (A/B) and the governing architectural principle: one largeness function, one ingest path, one gate site, reuse the existing [[DECOMPOSED]] handler, deprecate the Add-Idea(status='new') child path, and add no new goals.md or parallel approval gates. High reversibility, low cost, maximal simplicity. This atom is the explicit basis for rejecting atom_10's new gate.

From A only, but it specifies the planner contract that atom_02 and atom_06 depend on: emit both [[PROJECT_BACKLOG]] JSON (with required atom metadata) and [[DECOMPOSED:N]] markers. Consistent with atom_08's reuse of the [[DECOMPOSED]] handler. The dual-marker requirement carries mild redundancy (N is derivable from the JSON), which lowers simplicity; otherwise a necessary and concrete contract.

penalties.reason: Blocking conflict with consensus atom_04 and atom_08 (introduces a new approval gate, contradicting 'no new gates')

atoms.reason: From C only and flagged blocking. A mandatory operator review of the MAP/PLAN and atom list before auto-approval directly contradicts consensus atom_04 (children created approved) and violates consensus atom_08's explicit 'no new parallel approval gates', while defeating the bridge-self autopilot's purpose. Its legitimate concern — human oversight — is preserved more cheaply by atom_07 (operator-hold on retry exhaustion) and atom_11 (regression coverage). Reject as a standing gate; fold its intent into atom_07. Technically feasible and somewhat risk-reducing, but it loses on correctness, impact, and simplicity against the consensus.

From A only, but it is the verification counterpart to atom_05: mandatory regression tests proving PROJECT-channel non-interference and unchanged F1–F4 behavior. Purely additive, low cost, high reversibility, and high risk-reduction — it converts the isolation guarantee into a continuously checked invariant and partially substitutes for atom_10's oversight concern. Specificity would improve by naming the exact channels/cases to cover.
